ATTRIBUTED to a mechanism, from the player's own bytes. Read-only: I wrote nothing in the repo (git status shows only three sibling-owned modifications I did not make); every probe, workdir and scratch file went to the session scratchpad.

1. THE STATED CAUSE IS FALSIFIED FOR THIS FILE, AND THE FILE IS COUNTED BY THE SENTENCE.
build/fidelity.json row Skate_or_Die_intro.sid: drift_per_1000 = 200.0, drift_total = 498.0, drift_mad = 0.0, drift_span = 2490, drift_lag = 5.6, drift_voices = 3, and drift_gate_skip = True. So it is one of the 20 files that python/fidelity.py:4363 counts in "On 20 file(s) this is exactly -1/(skip+1)". Its skip is 127 (find_song_speeds gives SongSpeeds(frames=(3,), reload_addr=19219, table_addr=16350, skip=(127,), skip_table_addr=16346)), so the formula predicts -7.81 per 1000 against an observed +200.00 -- wrong sign, 25.60x magnitude.
I audited all 20 the sentence counts. 19 fit within 1% (After_8 -12.35 vs -12.35, Sanxion -9.17 vs -9.17, Ricochet -7.81 vs -7.81; loosest is Powerplay at 0.89). Skate or Die intro is the only miss, obs/pred = -25.60, and it is the largest-magnitude member of the set by 15x. The prose defect: _drift_gate_skip_declined (python/fidelity.py:3649) tests only that the file CARRIES the mechanism -- skip present, effective_frames declines the correction -- never that the observed value EQUALS the prediction, though its docstring calls it "the exact condition drift's docstring names as producing -1/(skip+1)".

2. THE MECHANISM: THE SPEED/SKIP TABLES ARE INDEXED BY $02A6, THE PAL/NTSC FLAG, AND WE READ THE NTSC ENTRY.
The file's init is at $3FE0 and its bytes (read out of the image) are AE A6 02 BD DA 3F 8D DD 45 8D 14 4B BD DC 3F 8D 01 48 BD DE 3F 8D 13 4B:
  $3FE0 LDX $02A6      ; 1 = PAL, 0 = NTSC
  $3FE3 LDA $3FDA,X    ; outer gate reload
  $3FE6 STA $45DD      ; self-modifies the LDA #imm at $45DC
  $3FE9 STA $4B14
  $3FEC LDA $3FDC,X / STA $4801
  $3FF2 LDA $3FDE,X    ; inner gate reload
  $3FF5 STA $4B13
Tables: $3FDA = [$7F, $04], $3FDC = [$FD, $F0], $3FDE = [$02, $01]. The index is the video standard, NOT the subtune -- but _speeds_for_reload takes vals = data[off:off+n] with n = subtunes = 1, and _find_outer_gate does the same, so both read entry 0. Entry 0 is the NTSC pair; the trace and the tune play PAL (run_siddump passes -vPAL, and sidfile reports speed field 0, RSID v2, not CIA).

Simulating the two counters over 5000 calls against the gate at $45D4 (LDX $4B15 / DEC $4B14 / BPL +8 / LDA #imm / STA $4B14 / JMP $45EF / DEC $4B12 / BPL +6 / LDA $4B13 / STA $4B12, with the fetch at $45F6 requiring $4B14 != 0 and $4B12 == $4B13):
  entry 0 (outer 127, inner 2): 3.0248 calls per tick, gaps 3 x1613 / 4 x39
  entry 1 (outer   4, inner 1): 2.5000 calls per tick exactly, gaps 2 x999 / 3 x1000
The PAL row alternates 2 and 3 calls and averages exactly 5/2 frames. 2.5 PAL frames (50.125 Hz) = 49.88 ms and 3.0248 NTSC frames (60.099 Hz) = 50.33 ms -- the same musical tempo on both machines, which is what such a table is for and an independent confirmation of which entry is which.

3. THE NUMBER FOLLOWS EXACTLY, AND IS CONFIRMED ON THE TRACE.
Emitted row 3.00 frames (CMD_SETTEMPO 3 at -S1) over a true row of 2.50 = 6/5 = +200.0 per 1000, MAD 0.0. fidelity.py --pace agrees independently: "our row 3.00 frames, ours/theirs 1.200 (IQR 1.200-1.200 over 826 gaps; least-squares fit 1.200)", "their row is 2.50 frames, where the gate was read as 3".
Gap histograms settle row-length vs rows-per-note (the ambiguity pace's own docstring warns about). Original: v0 196 attacks {5:48, 10:147}, v1 600 {5:599}, v2 225 {5:19,10:111,15:19,20:75}. Shipped conversion: v0 144 {6:44,12:99}, v1 499 {6:498}, v2 186 {6:15,12:92,18:15,24:63} -- exactly 6/5 at every multiple on every voice, so rows-per-note is already right (2) and only the unit is wrong. Re-converting with --tempo 5 packed at -S2 (row = 5 calls / 2 = 2.50 frames) reproduces the original's histogram exactly: v0 196 {5:48,10:147}, v1 599 {5:598}, v2 225 {5:19,10:111,15:19,20:75}. CAVEAT, stated because it matters: that build's pitches are wrong (voice 1 reads F#7 throughout) because I forced only the tempo while every rate table was still encoded for -S1 -- it is a timing demonstration, not a shippable candidate. A real fix must go through find_song_speeds so the whole conversion is built at -S2.

4. THE EXISTING MACHINERY WOULD GET IT RIGHT FROM THE PAL ENTRY.
SongSpeeds(frames=(2,), skip=(4,)) gives exact_row 5/2 = 2.5000, denominator 2 <= MAX_ROW_DENOMINATOR (10), effective_frames 5/2, recommended_multiplier 2 -- i.e. tempo 5 at -S2, the packing measured above. From entry 0 it gives exact_row 384/127 = 3.0236, encodable None, effective_frames 3, -S1. So this is not an encodability-cap limitation; it is a wrong table index.

Scanned all 95 corpus .sid files for an LDA table,X naming the detected speed or skip table with an LDX/LDA $02A6 within the preceding 24 bytes: 95 scanned, 0 errors, exactly 1 hit -- Skate_or_Die_intro.sid. A fix is confined to one file.

evidence:
THE DESIGN IS SETTLED AND COSTED; NOTHING IS EMITTED YET, AND THE TASK AS I WROTE IT UNDERSTATED THE PRICE. Its verify says the phase is 'computable at emit time ... no new player state', which is true and incomplete: a CMD_SETPULSEPTR is a property of the ORDERLIST POSITION, and Goattracker's patterns are global, so a pattern entered at k distinct phases needs k copies -- the same constraint _apply_boundary_ties solves with copies. That cost is what decides the feature and the verify did not name it.

MEASURED IT INSTEAD OF ESTIMATING IT, from the ORIGINAL's own trace (the pulse value on each note's attack frame, 120 s, 5_Title_Tunes sub 0):
  v1 adsr $5700  238 onsets  12 distinct  span 1216 ($900-$DC0)
  v2 adsr $4700  238 onsets  12 distinct  span 1408 ($880-$E00)
  v3 adsr $5830  375 onsets  12 distinct  span 1408 ($8E0-$E60)
and the flat records ($2400/$0400/$0690/$2800) take ONE value, $800, on every one of their 256 onsets -- so only the sweeping records need any of this.

THE ONSET SEQUENCE IS EXACTLY PERIODIC, which is the property that makes it buildable. Voice 1 repeats with period 12 over all 238 onsets and is a clean triangle -- 900 a00 ac0 bc0 c80 d80 dc0 cc0 c00 b00 a40 940 -- confirming the mechanism is a free-running triangle and not drift. Voices 2 and 3 repeat with period 44. An exact period means the phase sequence repeats WITH the music, so a pattern occurrence has the same phase on every loop iteration and costs NO copy; a copy is needed only where one pattern sits at two positions inside a single loop at different phases.

WHAT IT WOULD COST TO BUILD. A Goattracker pulse entry is (speed, target), not a per-frame width, so entering a leg part-way is not directly expressible: each triangle leg has to be SPLIT at every entry point the phases need, and CMD_SETPULSEPTR indexes a segment. 12 entry points for voice 1 and 44 for voices 2 and 3 is roughly 100 pulse-table entries for this one file against the 255-row table -- feasible, but that is one file of the 24 carrying this engine, and `_pulse_layout` already has an overflow fallback it reaches today.

Explanation (A) holds for all six: no note byte with bit 7 set reaches the actual converted patterns.

head: 576391e
evidence:
THE TASK'S PREMISE IS REFUTED AND THE CAUSE IS NAMED. W_A_R subtune 0 is not losing notes: it plays the RIGHT NOTES IN THE RIGHT RHYTHM at 8/3 the correct period, and `melody` -- a difflib ratio over a fixed 60 s window -- charges it for the music that falls outside the window. This is CLAUDE.md's 'a score is not a clock' case, and the corpus's third-worst melody row is it.

TWO CLAIMS IN MY OWN TASK TEXT WERE WRONG.
  (1) 'voice 2 makes 19 attacks against the original's 224 (92% of the notes missing)' -- the notes are not missing. Over the paired prefix the note NAMES are 19/19 IDENTICAL on both voice 2 and voice 3.
  (2) 'THE SHARPEST CLUE: our voices 2 and 3 have IDENTICAL attack frames ... two voices playing one stream is a track-table defect' -- they share attack FRAMES and not note names, which is two voices moving together rhythmically. That is ordinary music, not a defect, and it was the clue I told the next reader to start from.

THE MEASUREMENT. Gap sequences, voice 3, traced 60 s at -S4:
    original   4   5   4   5   72  18  18  18  72  72  72
    ours      12  12  12  12  192  48  48  48 192 192 192
Every gap is 8/3 of the original's. Across 18 paired gaps on each of voices 2 and 3, 14 are exactly 2.667 and the four outliers are 3.0 and 2.4 -- 12/4 and 12/5, the quantisation of an original that alternates 4,5 because its true row is 4.5 whole frames. The underlying ratio is uniform.

THE CAUSE, arithmetic rather than inference. Subtune 0's entry pattern (167, voice 1's first orderlist entry) carries row-0 command `0F09` = CMD_SETTEMPO 9, and a value under $80 sets all three channels (gplay.c:494). A row of 9 calls at -S4 is 2.25 frames. We MEASURE 6 frames per row = 24 calls. And `gplay.c:198` sets the default `cptr->tick = 6*multiplier-1` -- at multiplier 4 that is exactly 24 calls. So subtune 0 is running at GOATTRACKER'S DEFAULT TEMPO and its own CMD_SETTEMPO is not taking effect. 24/9 = 8/3, the ratio measured above, closed exactly.

WHY THE COMMAND DOES NOT EXECUTE IS NOT YET KNOWN, and that is what remains. It is present on row 0 of the pattern the orderlist enters on -- checked, the first entry is $A7 = 167 and it is a pattern number rather than a transpose or repeat -- so the obvious candidates (written to the wrong pattern; the orderlist entering somewhere else; row 0's column taken by another command) are all ruled out. The next places to look are gt2reloc's own `nosettempo` optimisation over the packed song, and whether a subtune whose entry pattern is SHARED had its tempo dropped by `apply_tempos`' contested-pattern branch (8 patterns carry a tempo for 8 subtunes, so none was obviously dropped, but the branch that drops rather than clones is `len(patterns) >= MAX_PATTERNS` and this file has 209).

Every number above came through the harness's own resolution (_preset_opts, resolve_subtune, table_calibration, run_siddump at the packed -S), never a re-derivation. `fidelity.py --pace` DECLINES this file ('only 39 matched gap(s) -- the two sides share too little material to time'), which is why the clock error had not been seen before: the tool built to answer exactly this question cannot answer it here, because difflib cannot match enough of a window that holds 1/2.667 of the music. The gap-ratio comparison above is what works when --pace declines, and is worth keeping as a technique.

`--diagnose` was run first as the repo requires: the correspondence is the identity and s1->o1, s3->o3, s5->o5 and s6->o6 all read 100%, so only subtune 0 is affected and the other seven are unhurt by whatever this is.

head: c376622
evidence:
THE MECHANISM IS NAMED AND THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES EXACTLY. `recommended_multiplier` is evaluated for SUBTUNE 0 ONLY, but a packed .sid carries ONE call rate for the whole file. Kings of the Beach's subtune 0 wants -S1; its subtunes 2, 4, 5 and 6 each want -S3, because their row is 8/3 frames. The file is packed at -S1, where a row must be a whole number of calls, so an 8/3-frame row is emitted as 3 -- and 3 / (8/3) = 9/8 = 1.125, which is EXACTLY the ratio --pace measures (ours/theirs 1.125, IQR 1.091-1.200 over 81 gaps, least-squares fit 1.125, MAD 0.4). The traced subtune is 4. drift +125.00 frames/1000 is the same number: 12.5% slow.

IT IS NOT ONE FILE. Censused over all 83 convertible files, 12 have a subtune needing a higher -S than the file is packed at:
    Delta        -S2 needs -S10    Monty       -S1 needs -S8
    Knucklebusters -S1 needs -S8   Wiz         -S1 needs -S8
    Dragons_Lair_II -S2 needs -S8  Star_Paws   -S2 needs -S8
    W_A_R        -S4 needs -S8     Flash_Gordon -S4 needs -S7
    Kings_of_the_Beach -S1 needs -S3   Tarzan  -S1 needs -S3
This is a general limitation nobody had named: the multiplier is a property of the FILE and the row length is a property of the SUBTUNE.

AND THE FIX IS MEASURED. Packing Kings of the Beach at -S3 instead of -S1, everything else held: wave 57.3 -> 72.8%, gate 11.0 -> 33.1%, adsr 99.7 -> 100.0%, melody/sequence/pitch all unchanged at 100%, attacks 84/84 both ways. Nothing is worse on any scored column.

Raising -S is safe in principle as well as in this measurement: at -Sm a row of f frames is f*m calls, so anything expressible at -S1 stays expressible; the bounds are GT_MIN_TEMPO (a row needs >= 3 calls) and the 7-bit tempo value.

head: d346fe8
evidence: THE ROW IS 5/2 AND THE CAUSE IS THE PAL/NTSC FLAG -- which is the standing hypothesis CLAUDE.md already carried FOR THIS EXACT FILE ('one gate picks its reload from the PAL/NTSC flag, which is the standing hypothesis this file carries for Skate or Die intro, found real somewhere else'). It was right. The init at $3FE0 is: LDX $02A6 (the KERNAL territory flag, 0 = NTSC) / LDA $3FDA,X / STA $45DD / STA $4B14 / LDA $3FDC,X / STA $4801 / LDA $3FDE,X / STA $4B13. Two of those three tables are the ones the gate readers ALREADY locate -- $3FDE is exactly find_song_speeds' reload_addr feed and $3FDA the outer gate's -- but both readers index them by SUBTUNE, and this player indexes by TERRITORY. One subtune, so index 0, so NTSC: speed table 02 01 read as 2 (frames 3) and skip table 7F 04 read as 127. That gave exact_row 384/127 = 3.0236, whose denominator MAX_ROW_DENOMINATOR refuses, falling back to a flat 3. PAL's entries are 1 and 4, so frames=2, skip=4 and the row is 2 x 5/4 = 5/2 = 2.50 frames -- denominator 2, well inside the cap, packing exactly as tempo 5 at -S2. WHY NOTHING HAD REACHED IT: this file installs its own IRQ, so its PSID header's playAddress is 0, and v0.5.402's rescue spellings are anchored at the play address and correctly DECLINE. The fix is one helper, _pal_ntsc_indexed, called by both readers -- the same 'give it a name every caller has to use' shape as pack_subtune.

Classifying every compensation row by whether ANY other voice plays a pattern of that length, over the whole seven-file population: IMMUNE files are Rikky 196/196 matched (100%), Sigma_Seven 14/14 (100%) and **Arcade_Classics 3/74 (4.1%)**; DAMAGED files are Powerplay 45/45 (100%, -2.9pp), Wiz 58/59 (98.3%), Sanxion 69/73 (94.5%, -19.9pp) and One_on_One 39/41 (95.1%, -37.0pp). Arcade_Classics is 96% MISMATCHED and completely immune while Powerplay is 100% MATCHED and damaged, so the proposed discriminator does not merely fail to separate the groups -- it points the wrong way on the extremes. A FIFTH CANDIDATE DIED CHEAPLY IN THE SAME PASS: the compensation writes `base+1`, so its RELATIVE size depends on the base, and a small base should hurt more. The bases do not separate either -- immune Rikky reads 4 frames and damaged One_on_One reads 4; immune Sigma_Seven and Arcade_Classics read 3 and damaged Sanxion and Wiz read 3. (Powerplay reads no inner gate at all and takes the fallback, which is worth noting but is not a discriminator on its own.)
verify_output: The within-file experiment on One_on_One, forcing compensation into ONLY length-matched then ONLY mismatched patterns by wrapping regrid_tempos and reverting the CMD_SETTEMPO pairs it wrote into excluded patterns -- the emitter untouched, so this stayed inside the task's read-only touches. NON-VACUOUS AND FAITHFUL: the `none` arm reproduces sha dcc01d3ea040 and the `all` arm fb673fa4ff04, which are the exact shas the v0.5.410 drain measured, and `all` reverts nothing. Measured in-process (an out-of-process fidelity run would convert with the UNPATCHED emitter and compare four identical arms): none 98.64% melody / 41 comps all 61.62% / 39 matched-only 68.53% / **2 mismatched-only 54.34%**. Two compensations do more damage than all forty-one, and the 39 the lead predicted would be harmless cost 30pp. CAVEAT STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: these three arms confound PLACEMENT with DOSE, because removing compensations also leaves the song under-corrected in net timing, and melody is a difflib ratio over a fixed 60 s window. So the within-file arms are suggestive only; the refutation rests on the CROSS-FILE table above, where every file is measured with its own full compensation set and there is no such confound.
notes: STILL NOT DONE: the verify asks for Rikky's immunity EXPLAINED, and five candidates are now dead without one surviving. Dead so far -- (1) the compensation dose, (2) file-level per-call pitch movement, (3) a harness subtune artefact, (4) cross-voice pattern geometry, (5) the base row length. DURABLE AND WORTH BUILDING ON: the classification harness is written and cheap, and it is the shape any successor should reuse -- wrap regrid_tempos, let it place, then revert the pairs you want excluded, and measure IN-PROCESS. THE ONE UNEXPECTED RESULT worth chasing next is the non-monotonicity: damage is not additive in the number of compensation rows, so 'which rows' matters in a way no dose argument can express, and any future A/B that varies the compensation SET is not comparing like with like. THE CANDIDATE I DID NOT REACH is what the other voices are DOING at the compensated moment -- not their pattern LENGTHS, which is what was tested here, but whether a note ONSET in voice 1 or 2 falls on the lengthened row. That needs cumulative row positions across three voices of differing pattern lengths, which is real work rather than a filter. NOTHING WAS WRITTEN IN THE TREE: this task is read-only in its touches and the only modified file is .claude/tasks/whattask.json, which is the plan /whattask wrote before this run.

AND IT WOULD NOT HELP, which is the finding. `fidelity_better`'s `keeps_notes` requires `cand[2] >= ref[2]` -- OUR raw attack count, with no margin -- and it gates EVERY acceptance term in the function. head: 8bb87e9
evidence: THE GUARD IS CORRECT AS WRITTEN AND THE PROPOSED WIDENING IS A CATEGORY ERROR. The task reads 'the guard checks the pattern it writes into, but CMD_SETTEMPO lengthens all three voices' -- both halves true, and they are about DIFFERENT THINGS. Overwriting a command column is this guard's job. The tempo reaching the other voices is a TIMING effect, and no column-occupancy test can address it: v0.5.408 already measured the command's mere PRESENCE at 0.0pp on both casualties (base+0, column occupied identically, row not lengthened), so the damage is the extra CALL, which declining columns cannot prevent. AND THERE IS NOTHING THERE TO CLOBBER. `exclusive` admits only patterns whose `where` is exactly {(k, 0)}, so voices 1 and 2 never play a pattern regrid writes into -- verified over all 12 files that ship --regrid by snapshotting `patterns` before the call and diffing after: 304 patterns actually written, every one with where == {(k, 0)}. A CROSS-VOICE GUARD WOULD ALSO BE ILL-DEFINED: 169 of those 304 (55.6%) are replayed -- Trans-Atlantic 100%, Bangkok_Knights 95.7%, Wiz's most-played pattern 14 times -- so 'what voices 1 and 2 are doing at the same row' has up to fourteen different answers, and answering it per position is exactly the per-copy cost this schedule is pattern-global to avoid (its docstring says so: 'a per-position schedule would need a copy per phase, the cost that stopped the pulse-phase work').
verify_output: A FALSE DEFECT OF MY OWN WAS CAUGHT AND IS THE REASON THIS IS TRUSTWORTHY. A first census reported 2 of 304 written patterns as ALSO played by voices 1/2 (Monty's 6, Nemesis's 0) -- a real-looking leak in the exclusivity filter, and both at suspiciously low indices. Re-measured from the filter's OWN reconstruction of `where` and both come back [(0, 0)]: my census was counting the byte AFTER GT_ORDER_RESTART as a pattern reference, which regrid's `operand` skip exists precisely to avoid. So the leak was mine, not the code's, and the correct figure is 304 of 304 exclusive. THE VERIFY: 'the guard consults voices 1 and 2 ... a test pins that a compensation row is declined when another voice is mid-effect there, and a corpus byte-hash names exactly the files that move' -- the first two clauses describe a change that must NOT be made, so the honest completion is the refutation plus the third clause. Corpus byte-hash against a clean export of HEAD 8bb87e9: 83 converted / 12 refused / 0 errors both sides, MOVED 0 -- exactly the files that should move for a comment-only change. tests/test_regrid.py 9 passed.
notes: LEFT UNCOMMITTED: python/h2g/patterns.py, +22/-0, COMMENT ONLY at the guard, so the next reader does not re-propose the same widening -- it records the category error, the 304-of-304 exclusivity check, the 55.6% replay figure that makes a positional guard ill-defined, and my own miscount, since a census that counts a restart operand as a pattern is a mistake worth naming where it would recur. The task's why_mode said 'the 12 adopting files must be re-measured'; they need not be, because no byte moved -- and that is checked rather than argued. RECORDED MODEL is `sonnet` and this ran on OPUS, which is the session. NOTE FOR THE REGRID CLUSTER: this is the SIXTH candidate cause killed for the --regrid collapse (after dose, file-level pitch movement, a harness subtune artefact, cross-voice pattern geometry and the base row length). The extra call remains the damage and its discriminator remains unknown; the untested candidate is still whether a NOTE ONSET in voice 1 or 2 falls on the lengthened row, which needs cumulative row positions across three voices.

head: ed7f7bc
evidence: ONE-LINE CAUSE, FIXED, AND THE FIX IS PROVEN END TO END. The original's voice 0 plays ZERO of those seven pitches in the 60 s window (11 D#3 in 180 s); the original's VOICE 2 plays 223 of its 347 attacks on exactly them. So pattern 9 is voice-2 material appearing as a leading entry in voice 0's orderlist.

verify_output: THE VERIFY IS NOT MET: Rikky's immunity is still not explained, so this stays partial. What it DID settle, and what a follow-up must not redo: 1. THE STANDING LEAD IS REFUTED IN ITS OWN TERMS. The lead was 'a lengthened row changes how far an IN-PROGRESS pitch movement travels'. A FIRST PROBE OF MINE COULD NOT SPEAK TO IT AND I NEARLY PUBLISHED IT AS THOUGH IT COULD: it measured `orig[v].bend`, the ORIGINAL's per-voice travel, where the lead is about OURS. Re-measured on our own side in both arms, the lead dies: SANXION VOICE 1 HAS bend 0 AND slides 0 IN BOTH ARMS -- no pitch movement whatsoever on our side or the original's -- and still loses 11 collapsed entries. One_on_One v2 moves bend 187880 -> 186400 (-0.8%) and slides 748 -> 742 while its collapsed count moves +11.6%, a factor of 14 apart; Powerplay v0 moves bend 166200 -> 166224, +0.01%, essentially flat. A mechanism cannot explain an effect it does not move with, and it certainly cannot explain one in a voice where the mechanism is absent. 2. THE NEW LEAD, OFFERED AS A LEAD AND NOT AS A FINDING, because this repo's most repeated error is publishing an explanation that fits the shape of a regression: TIES. A tie is siddump's note change with NO gate retrigger, and its delta tracks the damage almost one for one -- Sanxion v1 ties +9 against collapsed +11, One_on_One v2 +19 against +22, Powerplay v0 +6 against +4 -- while every immune voice measured runs ties <= 0 and collapsed <= 0 (Rikky -1/-1 on all three voices, Arcade 0/-11/-1 against 0/-2/0). It has a mechanism attached that predicts the ratio: a tie between two attacks renames the second, so the pair no longer collapses and the collapsed count rises by one per event. It also survives the Sanxion case that killed the old lead, since a tie needs no printed bend. THIS IS NOT YET CHECKED. The check this repo demands is to turn the proposed cause off and see whether the effect survives -- suppress the extra ties and confirm the collapsed count returns -- and that was not run. Do not adopt it until it is. 3. WHY IT IS STILL NOT AN ANSWER TO THIS TASK even if it holds: it explains the DAMAGE, not the IMMUNITY. It re-poses the question as 'why does a lengthened row admit an extra tie in these three voices and not in Rikky's', which is a sharper question than the one this task started with but is not the same as answering it.

An out-of-process fidelity run would have converted with the unpatched emitter and compared identical arms. (i) The orderlist walk did not LOOP, so One_on_One's voice 2 covered 4 of 168 lengthened rows and the first refutation of candidate 7 rested on FOUR SAMPLES. Looping takes coverage to 13416 and the conclusion happens to hold -- but it was luck, not method, and a 4-sample table printed with three decimals is exactly what this repo keeps mistaking for evidence. (ii) The per-voice pitch measurement read the ORIGINAL's bend when the hypothesis is about OURS; see the verify. Same family as the harness errors CLAUDE.md lists -- a probe re-deriving something the question already fixed. head: cb2011c
evidence: THE TASK'S TITLE IS WRONG AND BOTH READINGS IT NAMED ARE REFUTED. The orderlist is FAITHFUL and the fix is not in convert_tracks. (1) READING ONE -- an aliasing or off-by-one read of voice 0's list -- IS DEAD ON THE RAW BYTES. Hubbard's own voice-0 track list reads `80 | 00 x20 | 07 ...` and voice 2's reads `00 00 00 00 29 29 1B 1B 02 02 02 02 07 02 ...`. Pattern $07 (our GT p9) is genuinely IN voice 0's list, immediately after twenty plays of pattern $00, and it is genuinely in voice 2's as well -- the two lists are otherwise completely different, so this was never one voice's list read as another's. Our emitted `<F0><DF> p0 <D3> p0 p9 p3 ...` reproduces those bytes exactly, twenty repeats and all. (2) READING TWO -- a start position the player enters later -- IS ALSO DEAD, on the frames. The clock is right: startup_lag 6, and the other two voices line up within 3-6 frames (orig v1 first attack frame 2, ours 8; orig v2 390, ours 393). The original's voice 0 is SILENT until frame 2145. Ours sounds pattern 9's twenty notes at frames 1928-2102 and then joins the real music at 2132. So the original is ON pattern $07 across that same window and PRODUCES NO SOUND -- it does not skip the entry, it plays it silently. (3) WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS, confirmed exactly rather than by resemblance: voice 0 sounds **20 notes before its own first instrument**, pattern 9 has **20 notes with every instrument byte 0**, and the first instrument voice 0 ever names is instrument 3 in pattern 3 -- the pattern where the aligned music starts. The counts are not close, they are identical, and they are the same twenty notes.
verify_output: THE VERIFY IS NOT MET AND DELIBERATELY SO: it asks for a change in convert_tracks with a test in test_tracks.py, and that would be fixing a function that is behaving correctly. Nothing was written to python/h2g/. IT HAS NOW BEEN CHECKED AND IT IS NOT A COINCIDENCE. That task's own census recorded Bangkok_Knights 20 (voice 0); those are these twenty. Its conclusion stands for Delta_Mix-E-Load_loader, whose 8 pre-instrument notes it measured as EXACT (15 attacks against 15 on both affected voices, same frames within the lag), and that is precisely why the blanket fix is wrong: the condition is benign on one file and is the whole defect on another. WHY --initial-instrument DOES NOT FIX IT, already measured by that task: forcing it on Bangkok left voice 0 at ratio 0.87 / pitches 50% UNCHANGED TO THE DECIMAL while moving the file's bytes (sha c2afd5e7a9a8 -> a208e3cc5cfd) and costing wave 42.8 -> 40.5% and gate 64.1 -> 60.2%. That option hands the voice the instrument the player's index array STARTS it on, which for this file is evidently not one that sounds. The question is not which instrument to give the notes -- it is whether the player sounds them at all before it has loaded one. THE OPEN QUESTION, for whoever takes it: what does this player do on a note whose voice has no instrument loaded? Read it in the player rather than inferring it from the trace, because the trace only says 'no sound' and there are at least two ways to get that (no gate, or a waveform of $00). head: cb2011c
evidence: FIVE OF THE SEVEN REGISTER DEFICITS ARE ATTRIBUTED, ONE OF THEM PROVEN BY TURNING THE CAUSE OFF, AND THE WHOLE FILE'S DEFICIT IS VOICE 2. The notes really are exact -- --diagnose gives the identity correspondence with all three voices at ratio 1.00 / pitches 100%, so nothing here is about the notes. (1) adsr 69% IS --cut-release, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF IT. The file-level number hides that it is one voice: per-voice adsr is 94.4 / 94.4 / **18.6**. The instrument map named the cause without ambiguity -- GT 3 `$0730` 'we play it, the original does not' with 125 notes, and directly below, 'sounded by the original with no instrument of ours' `$0739` pulse, 125 notes. The SAME instrument and the SAME 125 notes, differing in the release nibble alone, which `--cut-release` zeroes and which this file's presets select. TURNED OFF AND RE-MEASURED rather than argued: adsr 0.6919 -> 0.9005, voice 2 0.187 -> 0.813, voices 0 and 1 unchanged to three decimals, and wave (0.9678), gate (0.7246) and melody (1.0000) ALL EXACTLY UNCHANGED. A cause that moves its own column by 21 points and nothing else is attributed, not merely correlated. (2) hold 0% IS THE `fetch` MECHANISM, 4 of 4 instruments, 100% -- confirmed twice, by --hold-census and by `sound_run_delta = -1` in the raw row. That is the documented next-note fetch running `gatetimer & $3f` calls early, and at `-S1` it is a whole frame, so this file is one of the ones where it is VISIBLE rather than one where it is absent. Corpus-wide, not this file's. (3) nrun 0% IS ONE COMPARISON. `noise_run_instruments: 1`, matched 0, orig_only 0, ours_only 0. A 0% built on a single instrument is not a rate, and the reason only one joins is the same key collision as (1): `noise_runs` keys on the ADSR pair, and --cut-release moves ours off the original's for every instrument it touches. This is the 'a degenerate match is not evidence' rule, and the verdict string said SUPPORTS. (2) TIE DENSITY DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE, measured over all 21 voices of the seven files. head: 01d80e6
evidence: THE 'ONE SEMITONE FLAT' READING IS CORRECT ABOUT THE NAMES AND WRONG ABOUT THE FREQUENCIES, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS. Measured on $D400/$D401 at each side's own attack frame, the renamed attacks differ by **1.5% to 3.1%**, not by a semitone's 5.95%: One_on_One voice 2 reads freq(off)/freq(on) = 1.0306 on every pair (G#4->G-4 7074->6864, C-5->B-4 8912->8647) and Powerplay voice 0 reads 1.0153 (G-5->F#5 13155->12957, D-5->C#5 9856->9708, A#4->A-4 7822->7704). So the two arms are a FRACTION of a semitone apart and siddump, which names the nearest note, rounds them to opposite sides of a boundary. The name gap is real; the pitch gap is a third to a half of it. AND ON THOSE PAIRS THE ARMS CONVERGE EXACTLY. Four frames after the attack the two sides hold BIT-IDENTICAL frequencies -- 8912 vs 8912, 11897 vs 11897, 7074 vs 7074, ratio 1.00000 -- so the note being played is the same note and only the frame siddump named it on has moved. The pitch is gliding into the note and the extra call samples it one step earlier along the ramp. SANXION AND RIKKY HAVE **ZERO** renamed attacks under this alignment, which is consistent with the split established last run: Sanxion's damage is event reordering within an unchanged 32-name set, so no rename exists for this measurement to find.
verify_output: STILL PARTIAL, AND THIS RUN'S OWN HEADLINE IS THE THING THAT STOPPED IT. The convergence result above rests on 4 and 7 pairs -- the ones difflib classified as `replace` -- and widening the alignment CONTRADICTS IT. Pairing each ON attack with the nearest OFF attack within 6 frames instead: One_on_One v2 gives 146 renamed of 371 paired with **64%** converging at +4 frames, Powerplay v0 gives 13 renamed with **15%**, and Sanxion v1 -- which had ZERO renames under difflib -- gives **279** with 29%. Two reductions of one signal, answers differing by a factor of four to six, and the small one was unanimous. That is exactly the case this repo records as 'when two reductions of one signal disagree by 5x, one of them is counting a different event' -- so NEITHER is reported as the answer. The likely cause is alignment quality: a +-6 frame nearest-match will pair attacks that are not counterparts at all (Sanxion going 0 -> 279 is the tell), while difflib's `replace` opcodes select only the cleanly-corresponding runs and may be picking the easy cases. Settling it needs an alignment that is checked rather than assumed -- the same difflib alignment `--diagnose` uses, extended to report insert/delete as well as replace, or a frame-tolerance swept until the pairing count stabilises. SO THE ADOPTION-RELEVANT CLAIM IS **NOT** ESTABLISHED. 'melody's collapse on these files is largely a measurement artefact' would change whether --regrid should be adopted on One_on_One and Sanxion, which is a live decision, and it is supported at 64% under one alignment and 15% under the same alignment on the neighbouring file. Do not act on it yet.

head: c381acd
evidence: ALL FOUR ATTRIBUTED, IN TWO GROUPS OF TWO, AND NONE OF THEM IS A PACING DEFECT. GROUP 1 -- THE WRONG SUBTUNE PAIR, already documented and here confirmed by the coverage figure rather than re-argued. Commodore_64_Music_Examples: coverage 10.2%, 63 matched gaps, melody 13.5%. Dragons_Lair_Part_II: coverage 8.1%, 44 gaps, melody 14.1%. CLAUDE.md records both as correspondence failures -- Dragons_Lair reads 14% on the diagonal and 88% at its real counterpart o9, Commodore_64 is a clean off-by-one s1->o0 at 93%. When the two sides are playing different music the 'matched' notes are spurious, so their gap ratios are meaningless and a wide spread is the expected reading. These two are already refused for COVERAGE as well, so the IQR is not even the binding gate. GROUP 2 -- difflib MATCHED THE WRONG REPETITION, which is the task's own second hypothesis and is now measured. Chicken_Song's 421 gap ratios cluster at **1.0x (48%), 2.0x (23%) and 0.5x (23%)** -- and the 2.0x and 0.5x counts are EQUAL AT 98 EACH. Rikky's 190 cluster at 1.0x (18%), 0.33x (16%) and 3.0x (11% across 3.03/2.94/3.06). Reciprocal factors in near-equal numbers is the signature of a note paired with the wrong repeat of a repeating figure: one matched a repetition early against one matched a repetition late. THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THAT READABLE. ACE_II, an independently-confirmed file with a fractional 8/3 row, spreads CONTINUOUSLY around 1 -- 1.0, 0.91, 1.1, 1.2, 0.83, which are 5/6 and 6/5 either side -- with no discrete factor-of-N cluster at all, and its per-band median is 1.000 in every band while the IQR falls monotonically with gap length (0.367, 0.191, 0.093, 0.011). Rikky's per-band MEDIAN instead moves 1.000 -> 2.031 -> 0.340 and Chicken_Song's 2.000 -> 1.000 -> 0.500. A correct conversion cannot have a different ratio at different gap lengths; quantisation noise can only widen the spread, never shift the centre.
verify_output: THE VERIFY ASKED THAT EACH OF THE FOUR BE ATTRIBUTED, and each is, with the two groups kept apart as it insisted. It also named Rikky as 'the one that fits no story' because its row is an INTEGER 4 frames at -S1, so the fractional-row explanation cannot apply -- correct, and the answer is that Rikky needs no fractional-row explanation: its spread is a matching artefact, and a matching artefact is indifferent to the row length. **A CORRECTION TO SOMETHING I WROTE EARLIER TODAY, and it is the point of this run.** In the pace-IQR record (same session, one task earlier) I noted that Rikky and Chicken_Song 'return a median of exactly 1.000 despite the spread' -- true, and I let it imply their pacing is confirmed. IT DOES NOT. The median is 1.000 BECAUSE the mis-pairings are reciprocal and cancel: 98 gaps at 2.0x against 98 at 0.5x. A symmetric matching failure produces exactly the same median as a correct conversion, so on these two files the median is not evidence of anything. That is a live trap for anyone reading --pace's number without its spread. AND IT VINDICATES THE BOUND SET ONE TASK AGO. These four are precisely the files still refused above MAX_PACE_IQR = 0.35, and this run says WHY that refusal is right rather than merely conservative: in every one of the four the matched notes are not counterparts, so the ratio is not a row length. The refusal is detecting a real failure of the instrument, which is exactly what its message claims ('a limit of THIS measurement, not a verdict on the conversion').
notes: READ-ONLY TASK, HONOURED -- every path in touches is `r:` and nothing was written; the tree carries only the previous task's fidelity.py/test_pace.py edits plus runs.jsonl. NO CHANGE IS PROPOSED and that is the finding. The obvious follow-up -- make --pace reject reciprocal-factor pairs, or require gap ratios to cluster -- would be a change to note matching, and note matching is shared with `melody` and `--diagnose`. Chicken_Song converts at 62% melody and Rikky at 98%, so if the pairing is wrong on Rikky's gaps it may also be wrong wherever else difflib aligns that tune. Worth knowing before anyone 'fixes' --pace in isolation. THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT DID IT is cheap and reusable and should be preferred over --diagnose for this question: bucket the matched gap ratios by the ORIGINAL's gap length and read the per-band MEDIAN. A correct conversion holds the median flat and narrows the IQR as the baseline grows (ACE_II: 1.000 in all four bands, IQR 0.367 -> 0.011); a matching failure moves the median between bands. That separates 'quantisation of a fractional row' from 'the wrong notes are paired' in one run, which neither the IQR alone nor the median alone can do. SHORT GAPS ARE NOT THE CAUSE, checked because MIN_DRIFT_BASELINE exists for exactly that hazard one function over: ZERO of the gaps in any of the three files measured is 2 frames or shorter.

head: 9dac92b
evidence: THE WINDOW IS REFUTED AND THE NON-ADDITIVITY SURVIVES -- both halves of the verify, in that order, as it demanded. (1) IT IS NOT THE WINDOW. The caveat was that removing compensations leaves the song under-corrected, so it runs fast, overruns a fixed 60 s window and is charged for the surplus. Measured directly: our attack count against the original's 537 falls MONOTONICALLY with dose -- +6, +6, +4, +1, +1, +0 -- so the compensation is doing exactly its job and the surplus vanishes at full dose. Melody over the same arms is 0.9864, 0.9864, 0.5164, 0.4546, 0.5225, 0.6162. Melody does not track the surplus; where the surplus is largest melody is BEST. A window artefact would put those two in the same direction and they are opposed. (2) THE DAMAGE IS NON-MONOTONE, not merely non-additive, which is stronger than the recorded finding. Sweeping the dose as strict SUBSETS -- each arm the previous plus more, which the v0.5.412 arms could not be since '39 length-matched' and '2 mismatched' are DISJOINT sets and cannot be compared as doses at all -- melody is flat at 0.9864 through the first compensation, collapses to 0.5164 at five, bottoms at **0.4546 at ten**, and then RECOVERS to 0.5225 at fifteen and 0.6162 at all forty-one. Adding more compensation past the trough makes the file BETTER. (3) SO A PARTIAL SET IS NOT 'LESS REGRID', IT IS A DIFFERENT AND INCOHERENT SCHEDULE. That is the reading the U-shape forces: the full schedule is a whole, and re-gridding part of a song leaves it timed one way for a stretch and another way after, which is worse than either consistent extreme. It answers the verify's closing clause directly -- every regrid A/B that varies the compensation SET is comparing unlike things, and the '2 rows cost more than 41' reading was that artefact rather than a fact about placement.
verify_output: A UNIT ERROR IN MY OWN SWEEP, FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THE CONCLUSION, and it is what reconciles this run with the recorded figures. `regrid_tempos` changes 82 rows on this file where the task says 41. They are not different counts: each compensation is a PAIR -- the lengthened row and the row that restores the tempo -- and I verified all 41 pairs are adjacent at even offsets ((0,22),(0,23), (0,43),(0,44), (1,22),(1,23) ...). So my sweep's unit was CHANGED ROWS, and an odd cut splits a pair, keeping a lengthening with no restore. The arms at 1 and 5 changed rows are therefore invalid and are discarded; the valid arms are 0, 1, 5, 10, 15 and 41 COMPENSATIONS, and the U-shape above is stated on those alone. Had I reported the odd arms the table would have carried two rows describing a state regrid can never produce. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. Regrid still genuinely hurts this file: 0.9864 -> 0.6162 at full dose is the known -37pp, and nothing here softens it. The finding is only that the damage cannot be attributed to a NUMBER of compensations, so no dose argument -- 'it is too many rows', 'reduce the compensation rate' -- can be right. WHY it hurts is separate and was measured earlier in this session under ties-not-pitch-travel: 146 renamed attacks whose frequencies differ by 1.5-3.1% at the attack frame and converge exactly four frames later, i.e. siddump naming a gliding note from a grid moved one call.
notes: READ-ONLY TASK, HONOURED -- all paths `r:`, nothing written but runs.jsonl. All arms in-process through convert() with regrid_tempos wrapped, so the two sides really are the two emitters; an out-of-process fidelity run would have converted with the unpatched tree. THE HARNESS IS THE REUSABLE PART and it is worth keeping: wrap `regrid_tempos`, deep-copy the patterns before calling the real one, diff after to recover the placements, then restore the 4 bytes of any (pattern, row) to be excluded. That gives an exact subset arm with no emitter change at all. It lives in ad_dose.py; rk_align.py has the capture half without the revert. **AND THE PAIR STRUCTURE IS THE THING TO CARRY**: anyone reverting placements MUST revert them two at a time, or the arm has a raised tempo that is never put back. The pairs are adjacent in placement order, so an even prefix is safe and an odd one is not. FOR THE DEPENDENT TASK regrid-and-no-test-restart-need-a-guard-or-a-documented-incompatibility: this closes off one whole family of guard designs. A guard that caps or thins the compensation COUNT cannot help -- the U-shape says a thinned schedule is worse than the full one -- so the choice really is all-or-nothing per subtune, which is what `presets.json`'s per-song `regrid` flag already expresses. head: b223eed
evidence: **THE CAUSE I PUBLISHED AT v0.5.419 IS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED HERE.** That commit message and this task's own verify both say Confuzion's voice 2 track list ends `FF 4B` -- an out-of-range restart operand of 75 in a ~39-entry list -- and that convert_tracks normalises the 'tune ended' signal away. There is no operand. Version 5's `$FF` is a BARE terminator, and the bytes I read as its operand are the NEXT VOICE'S LIST: voice 0's list is 36 bytes then `$FF` at index 36, and voice 1 begins at $0C58 with a gap of **0 bytes** -- the `02 02` after the `$FF` is literally voice 1's first two bytes, and voice 1's own dump starts `02 02 02`. I read across a boundary and called it a field. AND THE FIX THAT READING IMPLIED IS REFUTED TOO, which is why chasing it further would have been expensive. If `$FF` meant 'stop' in version 5, every version-5 original would stop. Traced all nine at 600 s: **1 of 9 stops** -- Confuzion at 305.08 s -- while 5_Title_Tunes, Battle_of_Britain, Commodore_64_Music_Examples, Devils_Galop, Gremlins, Hunter_Patrol, One_Man_and_his_Droid and Thing_on_a_Spring all loop past 600 s with 3450-9454 attacks. So `$FF` = restart at 0 is CORRECT for the dialect and `convert_tracks` is faithful on 8 of the 9. A dialect-wide change would have rewritten eight files to fix one. WHAT IS CONFIRMED, and it is worth having: the original really does stop, so this is not one of the six defects this project has found in the measurement rather than the converter. All three voices fall silent together -- voice 0's last attack at 305.08 s, voice 1 at 304.84, voice 2 at 305.08 -- and the 30-second histogram goes 150, 148, 216, 157, 152, 199, 190, 222, 215, 305, 58, then **zero for the remaining 295 seconds**. 2012 attacks and then nothing.
verify_output: NOT DONE: `len` is unchanged, no byte moved, and the task cannot close until the file-specific cause is found. What it has instead is a much smaller search space and one fewer wrong answer in circulation. THE QUESTION IS NOW EXACTLY THIS: what stops Confuzion and not the eight other version-5 files whose track lists it structurally resembles? Its `$FF` terminators sit where theirs do and mean what theirs mean. Candidates NOT yet tested, in the order they look cheapest: (a) the restart lands somewhere that produces no sound -- check what pattern the loop re-enters and whether it is silent, which would make the original 'stop' audibly while still running; (b) the three voices' lists are of different lengths, so the tune only coincides once and the player's own state (a counter, a subtune index) is left somewhere it does not recover from; (c) the rip itself ends -- Confuzion's PSID may simply have been captured as a single pass, in which case the ORIGINAL is the outlier and our looping conversion is not wrong at all, which would close this task by refutation rather than by a fix. (c) IS THE ONE TO TEST FIRST because it is the cheapest and because it would invert the task. Nothing measured so far distinguishes 'the tune ends' from 'this rip ends'. A LISTENER INDEPENDENTLY REPORTED THIS FILE TODAY as a speed mismatch, and that half stands: --pace reads our row 3.00 frames, ratio 1.000, IQR 1.000-1.000 over 295 gaps, drift +0.00, '0% out', with melody 100% and 298/298 attacks. Whatever the ending turns out to be, the tempo is exact and should not be touched.
notes: NOTHING WRITTEN TO THE TREE. python/h2g/tracks.py was rw: in touches and was NOT edited -- the change it would have taken is the one refuted above. presets.json, docs/FIDELITY.md and build/fidelity.json were rw: and none needed writing; `git status` is clean. **THE RETRACTION NEEDS TO REACH TWO PLACES BESIDES THIS RECORD**, because a wrong cause in a commit message is greppable and this repo's own rule is that such a message must be retracted where a grep for its own words will land: v0.5.419's message (`b223eed`) states the `FF 4B` reading as located fact, and this task's `verify` in whattask.json repeats it. The next /whattask regenerates the second; the first is history and is corrected here by naming it. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, since it is a repeatable one: I printed 64 raw bytes from a voice pointer and read the bytes after the terminator as belonging to that voice. Track lists in this format are PACKED END TO END with no padding -- the next voice's pointer is the previous list's last byte plus one -- so any dump that runs past a terminator is showing another voice's data. The check that catches it costs one line: compare the pointer arithmetic against the dump length, which is what finally settled it. THE ONE THING THIS RUN ADDS THAT IS CHEAP TO REUSE: `stopped_at` over a 600 s trace, applied per dialect, answers 'does this player's terminator mean stop or loop' empirically without reading any 6502 -- 9 files in about 20 seconds. That is a better first move than disassembly for any terminator question, and it is what refuted the dialect-wide fix here.

head: b223eed
evidence: THE TWO ALIGNMENTS ARE RECONCILED, AND THE ONE I SUSPECTED WAS WRONG IS THE RIGHT ONE. The disagreement was difflib-`replace` (4 and 7 pairs, 100% converging) against nearest-frame within 6 frames (146/13/279 renames at 64/15/29%). I had recorded the wide window as the likely culprit because Sanxion went from ZERO renames under difflib to 279 under it. THE CONTROL SETTLES IT AND IT EXONERATES THE WIDE WINDOW: pairing the off arm against ITSELF at every tolerance from 0 to 10 reports **0 renames on all three files**. The pairing never invents a rename. So difflib was not the conservative reading, it was the WRONG one -- it emits `replace` only for short mismatched runs, and these renames sit inside `insert`/`delete` blocks, so it saw 4 of 146. AND THE TOLERANCE IS CHOSEN BY A PLATEAU RATHER THAN PICKED. Sweeping One_on_One: paired 107, 178, 257, 342, **371, 371, 371** at tolerances 0-10 and renamed 18, 55, 95, 133, **146, 146, 146** -- it saturates at 4, having paired every one of the on-arm's 371 attacks, and nothing changes above it. That is a justified alignment. SANXION AND POWERPLAY NEVER PLATEAU (Sanxion paired 366/380/406 and renamed 243/254/280 through tolerance 10; Powerplay 24/30/34 and 11/13/15), so no tolerance is justified for them and their shares are NOT measured here. Only One_on_One is answered.
verify_output: **THE ARTEFACT IS 29% OF THE DAMAGE, NOT 64%**, and the difference between those two numbers is the finding. Measured directly rather than inferred: take the on arm, substitute the off arm's note name at every paired rename that CONVERGES within 4 frames (94 of them), and re-score the collapsed difflib ratio against the original exactly as `melody` does.     regrid OFF                            0.9920     regrid ON                             0.4685     regrid ON, naming artefact removed    0.6203 The loss is -52.35pp and removing the artefact recovers +15.18pp, so 15.18/52.35 = **29%** of One_on_One's melody loss is a naming artefact and **71% is real**. 64% OF RENAMES CONVERGE AND THEY ARE ONLY 29% OF THE LOSS, because `melody` is a collapsed difflib ratio and not a count of renames: the non-converging renames and the attack-count changes dominate what difflib charges. A share of one quantity is not a share of another, and reporting the 64% as though it were the answer would have overstated the excuse by more than double. SO THE ADOPTION QUESTION IS ANSWERED IN THE UNFLATTERING DIRECTION: --regrid genuinely hurts One_on_One and the artefact does not excuse it. Nothing here argues for adopting it there, which is what the earlier partial left open.
notes: READ-ONLY TASK, HONOURED -- all paths `r:`, `git status` shows only runs.jsonl. Both arms converted in-process with `regrid` toggled, so they really are the two emitters. THE METHOD IS THE REUSABLE PART, and it is two things, not one. A TOLERANCE SWEEP with a PLATEAU test says whether a frame-based pairing is justified at all -- and it correctly declines on two of the three files here rather than producing a number for them. A SELF-PAIRING CONTROL (one arm against itself) says whether the pairing invents what it reports; it cost one extra call per row and it reversed my prior. Either alone would have left the disagreement standing. FOR THE DEPENDENT TASK melody-may-be-misreading-attacks-that-land-mid-glide: the effect is REAL and is now sized on one voice of one file at 29%. That is the number to generalise from, not the 64%. Note it is a share of a LOSS, so it exists only where there is a loss -- on a file scoring 99% there is nothing for it to be 29% of, and the corpus-wide question is how many attacks are named from a frame whose frequency is still moving, which this run did not measure. SANXION IS STILL UNRESOLVED and should not be folded in: its pairing does not converge, its damaged voice has bend 0 and slides 0 in both arms (so no pitch is moving and the naming story cannot apply), and its note-name SET is unchanged at 32. It is a different mechanism from One_on_One's and has been since the split was first measured.

head: b223eed

evidence: **THE LISTENER'S REPORT IS ANSWERED AND THE DIRECTION IS SETTLED: NO VOICE OF OURS IS LOW, IN ANY SUBTUNE.** The report was 'voice 2 arps too low'. Not one voice sits lower. Exactly ONE voice in the whole file has wrong notes at all -- subtune 0, voice index 1 -- at 41% of its attacks alien, and it is HIGH. Every other voice of every other subtune is 0% alien with an exact median. WORTH KEEPING ABOUT THE STATISTIC: the median would have MISSED this entirely. It reads 55.0 on both sides for the damaged voice, because only one note moved and the median note is not it. The alien-share is what found it. A median is the right guard against a clamp dragging a mean, and it is the wrong detector for the clamp itself -- both were computed, which is the only reason the row is readable. CONFIRMED ON FREQUENCIES, not on siddump's note names: at its first B-5 attacks the ORIGINAL writes $4315 and $4141, nearest the player's own table index **71 = B-5** ($41B8); at the corresponding attacks OURS writes $DD0E, nearest index **92 = G#7** ($DD08). 92 is $5C exactly -- the value of the clamp at patterns.py:495, `if g_note >= 0x5C: g_note = 0x5C`.
verify_output: NOT DONE -- no fix, and the mechanism is NOT where this task assumed. What is now excluded is worth more than what is left. THE RAW BYTES THE CLAMP SWALLOWS, recorded by instrumenting it and reverting immediately: $5D x4, $5F x4, **$68 x50**. Commando's frequency table is at $5428 with **96 entries** (shift 0, detune -0.06, negligible). So $5D and $5F are indices 93 and 95 -- REAL notes, A-7 and B-7, which Goattracker's range genuinely cannot hold, and clamping those eight is defensible. **$68 IS 104, EIGHT ENTRIES PAST THE END OF THE TABLE**, and the bytes there read $0000 -- silence. So the player cannot be sounding B-5 from a straight index-104 lookup, and the obvious fix (read past the table and map the frequency to the nearest note) would emit silence, not B-5. AND THERE IS NO TRANSPOSE IN THE NOTE READ. 104 - 71 = 33 invites a per-voice transpose, the shape detect.py already rescues for Auf Wiedersehen Monty (`CLC / ADC transpose,X` spliced into the idiom). Searched five spellings of the note-read idiom in Commando: only the PLAIN one matches (`C8 B1 ?? 9D ?? ?? 0A A8`), and mask-only, mask+transpose, transpose-without-mask and store-then-transpose all find nothing. `det.note_flag` is False and that is correct. SO THE REMAINING HYPOTHESIS IS THE ONE THIS TASK DID NOT CONSIDER: **our pattern walk is reading the wrong byte at those 50 slots.** If $68 is an instrument or command byte that we take as a note, everything above follows -- the player never looks it up, the table's end is irrelevant, and the note it really plays is a different byte entirely, index 71. That is testable directly: dump the pattern rows voice 1 of subtune 0 plays and check what our walk calls a note against what the player's own reader would take. Do that BEFORE touching the clamp -- the clamp is emitting 92 faithfully from a byte it should never have been given.
notes: NOTHING LEFT IN THE TREE. patterns.py was instrumented to record what the clamp swallowed and RESTORED FROM A BACKUP IMMEDIATELY -- `git status python/h2g/patterns.py` is clean, checked. goatwriter.py, presets.json, docs/FIDELITY.md and build/fidelity.json were all rw: in touches and none was written. FOR THE LISTENER: there is no subtune of Commando where a voice plays low. The one real pitch defect is 96 attacks on subtune 0's middle voice coming out at G#7 -- the top of Goattracker's range -- where the original plays B-5. If what was heard was an arpeggio figure sitting wrong rather than one note being high, that is consistent: 41% of that voice's attacks are the ceiling note, so the figure's shape is destroyed even though its other notes are exact. 50 CLAMPED SLOTS SOUND 96 TIMES because patterns replay; do not read a mismatch between those two counts as a second defect. AND DO NOT 'FIX' THE $5D/$5F CLAMPS. They are A-7 and B-7, inside the player's table and outside Goattracker's range, so clamping is the only available answer for those eight and changing it would be inventing a note.

An attack counts when the note siddump would name at the attack frame differs from the one it would name four frames later -- i.e. the pitch crosses a naming boundary while the note sounds. **IT IS A POPULATION AT RISK, NOT AN ERROR RATE**, and the record says so in those words because the two are a factor of several apart. Where both sides glide identically the names agree and nothing is lost. What the 31.7% bounds is the population in which a grid moved by one play call can rename a note that did not change -- and the one place that has been measured end to end is One_on_One under --regrid at v0.5.420, where it accounted for 29% of the file's melody loss.

notes: LEFT UNCOMMITTED: python/fidelity.py (the Dimension description plus a comment block carrying the census), python/tests/test_fidelity.py (+1 test), docs/FIDELITY.md (regenerated). build/fidelity.json was regenerated too and is gitignored. presets.json was `r:` and untouched. head: 89df05e
evidence: **THE GATE IS FOUND AND IT IS NOT A CONDITIONAL -- IT IS AN AND MASK, which is why the previous run's search for 'a branch between the frequency write and the $D404 write' could not have succeeded.** Bangkok's per-frame voice update reads:   $8536 LDY $85AB          ; the voice's SID offset   $8539 LDA $85B8,X        ; the voice's stored waveform   $853C AND $85C1,X        ; <-- MASKED HERE   $853F STA $D404,Y        ; waveform   $8542 LDA $863F,X / STA $D401,Y    ; freq hi, unconditional   $8548 LDA $8674,X / STA $D400,Y    ; freq lo, unconditional So the waveform written is `$85B8,X AND $85C1,X` while BOTH frequency writes happen regardless, immediately after and with no branch between them. That is exactly the trace's shape -- pitch written, $D404 left at $00 -- and it means the thing to look for was never a conditional at all. AND THE OTHER $D404 SITE IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM, worth recording so it is not chased again: $83E0-$840D is the WAVE PROGRAM interpreter, not the note path. `LDA ($F8),Y / BPL` splits it -- bit 7 SET writes the waveform and an absolute frequency ($83FC/$8402), bit 7 CLEAR falls to $8410 and SUBTRACTS from the frequency accumulator with SBC ($F8),Y into $8674,X and $863F,X. That is the `set`/`slide` opcode pair CLAUDE.md documents for `_wave_program_entries`, appearing here in its own player.
verify_output: STILL PARTIAL, and the honest limit is which of the two masked cells is zero. The trace proves `$85B8,X AND $85C1,X` evaluates to $00 across those 20 notes; it does NOT say whether the stored waveform or the mask is the zero one. I did not settle it, and the obvious shortcut is barred: the FILE IMAGE has $85B8 = 09 0D D0 and $85C1 = 10 68 11 for the three voices, both non-zero -- but these are mutable player state, so the image is where the RIPPER left them, not where init does. That is the same trap `initial_instruments` sets, recorded in tracks.py's own comment. TWO WRITERS OF $85C1 EXIST, at $815A and $8248, and reading those two is the next step -- if one is the instrument load then the mask is the gate and the rule is 'no instrument, no waveform'. THE CHEAPER ROUTE, and probably the right one: patch a copy of the .sid to redirect one of the two loads into $D404 and trace it, the way CLAUDE.md records the Ninja bit-$02 threshold being settled ('redirecting one LDA printed the counter into $D404, where it read 1 1 2 3 4 4 5 and named the gate'). That answers which cell is zero in one run and needs no further disassembly. DELTA IS UNTOUCHED THIS RUN and remains the constraint that makes this hard: its voice 0 holds instrument 3's waveform and ADSR from FRAME 1, so whatever rule is emitted must silence Bangkok's 20 pre-instrument notes and leave Delta's 8 exact.
notes: NOTHING WRITTEN TO THE TREE. This task holds rw: on three h2g modules and none was edited; `git status` shows only runs.jsonl. A NOTE ON THE TOOL, since it cost two passes: my scratch disassembler had a complete INSTRUCTION-LENGTH table and an incomplete NAME table, so the first output rendered the interesting instructions as raw bytes (`.AC`, `.AE`, `.3D`, `.B1`) while stepping over them correctly. The lengths being right is what made the second pass a pure re-render rather than a re-derivation -- but a disassembler that silently prints `.B1` for `LDA (zp),Y` in the middle of the one idiom being read is a tool that hides its answer. Fill both tables together. ALSO: disassembling BACKWARD from a known store by a fixed byte count lands mid-instruction and prints convincing nonsense -- the first attempt rendered 12 lines of `.00`/`.14`/`.80` from the middle of a data table. Always disassemble FORWARD from an address believed to be an instruction boundary, and pick that address from a branch target or a subroutine entry rather than by subtracting 40.

head: 89df05e
evidence: TWELFTH CANDIDATE DEAD -- and this one was mine, proposed and refuted in the same run. THE HYPOTHESIS was that --regrid's damage is renaming (established at v0.5.420: 29% of One_on_One's loss is a naming artefact) and that Rikky is immune because its attacks cannot BE renamed. The corpus mid-glide census from v0.5.421 tests it for free -- it already says, per file, what share of attacks are named from a frame whose pitch is still moving, which is exactly the population a grid shift can rename. IT DOES NOT SEPARATE THE GROUPS, and it fails at both ends:     Rikky            0.0%  immune          Powerplay      **0.0%  DAMAGED -2.9pp**     Sigma_Seven      0.0%  immune          One_on_One      17.5%  DAMAGED -37.0pp     Wiz             22.0%  immune          Sanxion         24.3%  DAMAGED -19.9pp     Arcade_Classics **41.7% immune** Arcade_Classics has the highest mid-glide share of the seven and is immune; Powerplay has ZERO and is damaged. And the share does not even predict severity -- One_on_One, the worst hit at -37pp, sits at 17.5%, BELOW the corpus median of 24.3%.
verify_output: STILL PARTIAL -- Rikky's immunity is not explained, and this is the twelfth candidate to fail. But the refutation is sharper than a null and leaves two things worth having. **(1) THERE ARE AT LEAST TWO DAMAGE CHANNELS, and Powerplay proves it.** Powerplay has 0.0% mid-glide attacks, so NONE of its -2.9pp can be a naming artefact -- there is no population for the artefact to live in. That independently confirms the v0.5.420 measurement, which found only 15% of Powerplay's renames converging against One_on_One's 64%: two files, two mechanisms, and the numbers agree from opposite directions. Any single explanation for all three damaged files is now excluded twice over. **(2) RIKKY'S NAMING CHANNEL IS CLOSED, which is a necessary condition and not a sufficient one.** At 0.0% mid-glide it cannot be damaged by renaming, which is consistent with its ZERO renames under difflib at v0.5.420. So one of the two channels is accounted for. The other -- whatever costs Powerplay its 2.9pp with no renaming available -- is still open for Rikky, and that is now the whole of the remaining question. THE QUESTION IS THEREFORE NARROWER THAN IT WAS: not 'why is Rikky immune' but 'what is the non-naming damage channel, and why does it not reach Rikky'. Powerplay is the right file to study it on, because it carries that channel ALONE and uncontaminated -- 0% naming, all real.
notes: READ-ONLY, nothing written but runs.jsonl. This run cost one query: the mid-glide shares were already computed and stored at v0.5.421 (scratchpad mg_size.json), so testing the hypothesis was a join rather than a measurement. Worth noting because it is the argument for writing a census to disk rather than printing it -- the file answered a question it was not built for. THE TWELVE DEAD CANDIDATES, so none is retried: compensation dose; file-level per-call pitch movement; a harness subtune artefact; cross-voice pattern geometry; base row length; the occupied-column guard; per-voice pitch movement in the original; onset-on-the-lengthened-row; the in-progress-pitch-travel lead; the tie positional test (vacuous); tie density; and now mid-glide share. AND ONE STANDING RESULT THAT IS NOT A CANDIDATE: the damage is NON-MONOTONE in the dose (v0.5.418), so a thinned compensation schedule is worse than the full one and no guard that caps the count can help. Whatever the channel turns out to be, the remedy is per-song all-or-nothing, which presets.json's `regrid` flag already expresses.

evidence: **HALF A STEP FORWARD AND ONE FALSE POSITIVE CAUGHT BEFORE IT BECAME A DETECTION.** WHAT HOLDS: the idiom that decides whether a pre-instrument note sounds is locatable by signature. `LDA abs,X / AND abs,X / STA $D404,Y` (`BD ?? ?? 3D ?? ?? 99 04 D4`) is Bangkok's $8539, and searching for it finds the same shape -- and with it the per-voice stored-waveform cell, the operand of the LDA -- in four of six files tried: Bangkok $85B8, Delta $C52F, Dragons_Lair_Part_II $C4D4, ACE_II $E559. Gremlins and Commando carry a different shape and are not reached by it. That is a real, reusable locator for the cell v0.5.424 identified as the gate. **WHAT DOES NOT HOLD IS THE DISCRIMINATOR BUILT ON IT.** The proposed test was 'does the init routine write that cell' -- Bangkok's is never written (so its pre-instrument notes are silent), Delta's should be (so its eight sound). The scan returned exactly one YES, Delta at $C032 -> $C52F, which is the answer the hypothesis wanted. **IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE.** $C032 lies inside the PSID metadata: $C010-$C05F reads 'Delta Mix-E-Load (loader) ... Rob Hubbard ... 1987 Thalamu'. My init walker had desynchronised into ASCII and read a filename byte as `STA abs`. THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, not a slip: `sid.data` is the WHOLE file including the PSID header (the header length computes to 0, checked at v0.5.424), so `load_addr + offset` maps the header's strings into the address space as though they were code. Any walk that steps into a low address disassembles the tune's title.
verify_output: STILL PARTIAL, and the discriminator is UNVERIFIED rather than established -- which is the opposite of what the table said before I read $C032's neighbourhood. No emitter change; the verify's requirements are untouched. **AND A PREVIOUSLY REPORTED FIGURE IS NOW SUSPECT FOR THE SAME REASON.** Two runs of this task ago I used the same bounded init walker to conclude that neither Bangkok nor Delta writes $D404-$D406 at init, and reported alongside it that '26 of the 95 corpus files DO' as evidence the probe worked. That number came from the same walk and may include files where it wandered into header text. The conclusion it supported -- that Delta's instrument arrives at the first PLAY call rather than at init -- is independently confirmed by the trace (voice 0 holds $41 and $3A98 from frame 1, and frame 1 is the first play call), so that reading survives; the 26 does not, and should not be quoted. WHAT A CORRECT VERSION NEEDS: a walk that knows where CODE begins. The PSID header is not part of the C64 image, and `sid.to_offset` is the function that already knows the mapping -- the walker should refuse any address that resolves below the first code byte rather than silently disassembling it. That is a fix to the probe, not to the converter, and it is worth making before the discriminator is trusted, because the hypothesis and the artefact predict the SAME answer here and only the artefact is cheap to produce.

head: 82e2d48
evidence: **THE NOTE BYTE IS CONFIRMED FROM THE CONVERTER'S OWN READER, AND THE PLAYER CANNOT BE USING IT AS A TABLE INDEX.** The last run withdrew its ad-hoc parse, so this took the bytes from `convert_patterns` itself -- the clamp instrumented to log every byte it pins, the file reverted afterwards and hashed identical (2b4a83adb731). Commando clamps **58 notes across 5 patterns**: **$68 x50**, $5D x4, $5F x4. So the eyeballed `$68` survives even though the aggregate table around it did not. **$68 IS 104 AND THE PLAYER'S FREQUENCY TABLE HAS 96 ENTRIES.** `find_freq_table` reads it at $5428, length 96, shift 0, detune -0.062, run 95 -- and the table is confirmed correct by a direct hit: entry $34 (52) is **$15EB**, which is EXACTLY the median $D400 of the original's 81 E-4 attacks. Entry $68 reads **$0000** -- past the end, silence. The original does not play silence there. **WHAT IT DOES PLAY IS INDEX 71.** Its 95 B-5 attacks cluster at mode $4341, spread $4115-$4381. Table entry 71 is $41B8, inside that spread; entry 72 is $45A0, ABOVE its maximum. And 71 is B-5 in the same numbering that makes entry 52 the traced E-4. So the sounded pitch is table index 71 while the pattern byte is 104.
verify_output: STILL PARTIAL -- no emitter change, the clamp is untouched and `len`/melody are unmoved. Two candidate mechanisms are now DEAD, both killed by measurement rather than argument. (1) **AN ORDERLIST TRANSPOSE APPLIED AFTER THE CLAMP.** 104 - 71 = 33, so a -33 transpose would explain it exactly, and the clamp runs at pattern-decode time while transposes are applied later -- a genuinely attractive story. It is false: `convert_tracks(..., transposes=tp)` returns **nine empty maps** for this file. Commando's orderlists carry no transpose at any position, so there is nothing arriving later to rescue a clamped note. (2) **THE COMMAND BYTE SELECTS THE INTERPRETATION.** The last run's reading was that `$81` changes how the following note bytes are read while `$83` does not. Attributing the original's attacks by the ADSR pair at the attack frame **inverts that**: the 95 B-5s all carry `$0FC4`, which is record **4** (`00 02 43 0F C4 00 00 03`), and every melodic note -- E-4 x81, G-4 x28, F-4 x16, D-4 x12, G#4 x4 -- carries `$064B`, which is record **1** (`80 01 41 06 4B 00 00 05`). Since `$81` and `$83` are instrument selects, the notes that clamp are NOT the ones the eyeballed dump put after `$81`. The command-to-note pairing in that dump does not survive, exactly as its own record warned it might.
notes: NOTHING LEFT IN THE TREE. patterns.py was instrumented under my declared `rw:` and restored; sha256 of the restored file equals the pre-run backup, and `git status` shows only runs.jsonl. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD DO, and it is now a single well-posed question: **what does the player do with a note byte for record 4?** Record 4's effect byte is $03 (bits $01|$02) against record 1's $05 ($01|$04), and its byte 0 is $00 where records 1, 2, 5 and 7 carry $80 -- so the two populations differ in the record, not in the pattern command. The behaviour to explain is that a byte of 104 sounds table index 71, consistently, 95 times. Read record 4's path in the player; do NOT re-derive the pattern parse, which has now been wrong twice. A CONSTRAINT ON ANY FIX: the clamp `g_note >= 0x5C -> 0x5C` is not itself the defect. It is right for the 8 marginal bytes ($5D, $5F) and it is what keeps every other note on this voice exact. Whatever replaces it must be conditioned on the record, and Commando is the byte-exact fixture -- `Commando.sng` must still reproduce byte for byte unless the fixture is deliberately re-cut, which is a much larger decision than this task. That constraint was not stated in the task and is the single biggest thing standing between a diagnosis and a shipped fix here.

head: 9b382b9
evidence: **THE TASK'S TITLE IS BACKWARDS, AND THE RULE IS ALREADY CORRECT EVERYWHERE.** Measured over all 83 convertible corpus files: **0 files** pack for a subtune other than the one they start on -- `pack_subtune(speeds, sid.start_song)` equals `fidelity.resolve_subtune(path, 'auto')` on every one -- and **0 files** ship a `presets.json` multiplier differing from `recommended_multiplier` at that subtune. The v0.5.410 rule is applied consistently and the artefact agrees with it. WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS is the reverse and `pack_subtune`'s own docstring already states it: files whose NON-STARTING subtunes are served at the wrong rate. That is not a defect in the rule but a property of one packed file having one call rate -- a row of p/q frames is exact only at multiples of q, so a rate exact for every subtune is the LCM of their denominators (24 for Monty and Knucklebusters, 40 for Delta and Wiz, **140 for Flash Gordon**) against a MAX_ROW_DENOMINATOR of 10. Per-subtune rates need a file per subtune, which is a different feature. **THE DOCSTRING'S FIGURES RE-VERIFY EXACTLY**, which is worth saying after five stale figures this session: 12 corpus files have some subtune wanting a higher multiplier than subtune 0, and exactly **2** have a START subtune that does -- Kings_of_the_Beach_ingame (s4, 1 -> 3) and Knucklebusters (s1, 1 -> 3). So its 'the other ten files' is right. My own table counts **13**, which is not drift: it uses a broader predicate (any subtune differing from the PACK subtune's rate in EITHER direction, which also catches subtunes wanting less). Both numbers are correct under their own definitions and neither supersedes the other.
verify_output: The verify asked that each of the ten be named with its startSong and the subtune actually packed, and that any that are wrong be corrected. None is wrong, so nothing was corrected and no artefact needed regenerating -- presets.json, SURVEY.md, SUBTUNES.md, FIDELITY.md and build/fidelity.json were all `rw:` in my touches and none was written. **WHAT I ADDED INSTEAD IS THE MISSING TEST.** The two existing corpus tests pin only the two files the rule MOVED, against hard-coded expectations. The corpus-wide invariant -- whose failure mode is documented as silent and severe (Las Vegas converting to SILENCE, Samantha Fox playing three times too fast, both with melody still reading 100%) -- was not pinned at all. Two tests now in tests/test_pack_subtune.py: `test_no_corpus_file_packs_for_a_subtune_it_does_not_start_on` (pack_subtune agrees with resolve_subtune on every file, with the documented fall-back to 0 where a header over-declares past the speeds table), and `test_every_derivation_site_agrees_on_every_corpus_file` (presets, fidelity and convert checked against EACH OTHER on every tune, with no expected value that can go stale). **BOTH PROVEN NON-VACUOUS, BY TWO DIFFERENT PERTURBATIONS, AND THE SECOND ONE MATTERED.** Reverting `pack_subtune` to the pre-v0.5.410 'always subtune 0' fails the first test -- but the second one PASSES under that same revert, correctly, because all three sites call `pack_subtune` and therefore move together and still agree. It checks mutual agreement, not the rule. Its real check is one site drifting, so I perturbed `_derived_multiplier` alone: it then fails with `Kings_of_the_Beach_ingame.sid: presets 3, fidelity 3, convert 1`, which is exactly the Las Vegas shape. Both files restored; tests/test_pack_subtune.py 8 passed in 17s.
notes: LEFT UNCOMMITTED: python/tests/test_pack_subtune.py only (+2 tests). No source file changed, so no conversion moved and no byte-hash is needed. **THE NON-VACUOUSNESS STEP NEARLY LIED TO ME AND THAT IS THE LESSON.** My first attempt ran the whole test file with `-x` under the revert, saw `1 failed`, and would have been recorded as proof. It stopped on `test_start_song_is_one_based` -- a PRE-EXISTING test -- and said nothing whatever about the two I had just written. A non-vacuousness check must name the test it is proving and run THAT ONE; `-x` over a file actively defeats it by stopping before your test runs. Same family as this repo's 'asserting a prefix of the match is not asserting the match'. AND THE SECOND TEST'S LIMIT IS NOW ON THE RECORD rather than assumed: it cannot see a change to the shared rule, only a divergence between the sites. That is the right scope for it -- the first test covers the rule -- but a reader who assumed it covered both would be wrong.

head: 9b382b9
evidence: **THE VERIFY'S FIRST BRANCH IS DEAD AND ITS SECOND IS UNCHANGED, SO A THIRD THING WAS DONE.** The verify offered: skip the toggle on `no_hard_restart` songs, or add a `fidelity_better` term that reads it. The first is impossible -- `no_hard_restart` is in presets.json's `always` block, so it is true of ALL 83 songs, and v0.5.429 measured the supposedly dead axes as live on 15 and 14 of them. Skipping there would delete real axes from the search. The second is a scoring change needing two full corpus searches to adopt, which is not a one-iteration job. **WHAT IS SOUND AND IS NOW IMPLEMENTED IS A DIFFERENT PRUNE, AND IT IS MEASURED BOTH WAYS.** With `max_hard_restart` FORCED ON across the corpus, `wide_hard_restart` changes the conversion on **0 of 83** files -- max takes the player's own limit, which supersedes the width. With max forced OFF it changes **36 of 83**, which is the converse that says the toggle is worth having and this is not merely deleting a dead option. So `{max=True, wide=True}` is byte-identical to `{max=True, wide=False}`, a combination the walk still visits, and skipping it cannot change what the search selects. `presets._redundant_combination` does that: **32 of the 127 combinations a song**, a quarter of the walk, each of which is a convert, a pack and two traces.
verify_output: PARTIAL: `hard_restart_frames` itself is still not searchable -- nothing added a term that reads it, which is the task's actual title. What landed is a saving on the walk that carries it. SUITE: **1660 passed, 2 skipped** (1656 before, plus the 4 tests added this cycle). **NON-VACUOUSNESS, STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE IS**: with `_redundant_combination` reverted to `return False`, `test_the_only_pruned_combination_is_wide_under_max` FAILS -- it asserts the prune skips something. The other two PASS under that revert and both are correct to. `test_no_combination_without_max_is_pruned` is a converse GUARD against a future widening of the predicate, and 'nothing outside max is pruned' holds trivially when nothing is pruned at all. And `test_a_candidate_that_will_not_convert_is_skipped_not_fatal` passes because I deliberately made its count derive FROM `_redundant_combination` rather than restate it -- so it adapts instead of detecting, which is the right design and also means it cannot serve as this proof. Claiming all three as non-vacuous would have been the exact error I made on this task's neighbour an hour ago. **I BROKE A PRE-EXISTING TEST AND IT WAS THE RIGHT TEST TO BREAK.** `test_a_candidate_that_will_not_convert_is_skipped_not_fatal` asserted `raising == 2**(n-1)` = 64 and got 48, because 16 of the two_stage-carrying combinations are now pruned. Its own comment says a number restating what the module declares drifts from it -- so the fix keeps that principle and counts the surviving combinations through the predicate instead of hardcoding 48.
notes: LEFT UNCOMMITTED for this task: python/presets.py (+35, the predicate and its reasoning), python/tests/test_presets.py (+41, two tests), python/tests/test_preset_passthrough.py (+12/-2, the derivation). Alongside earlier tasks in this cycle: python/fidelity.py and python/tests/test_pack_subtune.py. **NO CONVERSION MOVED AND presets.json WAS NOT REGENERATED.** The change is to the SEARCH, not to `convert()`, and the artefact records a previous search's selections; a regeneration is a separate, 8-minute decision that also re-runs every song's walk. presets.json, docs/FIDELITY.md and build/fidelity.json were `rw:` in my touches and none was written. WHY THE PRUNE IS SAFE IN A WAY A PLAUSIBILITY PRUNE WOULD NOT BE, recorded in the docstring so the next person widening it has the rule: a combination may be skipped ONLY when one still visited produces the same BYTES. `fidelity_better` is not a total order and the greedy path's outcome depends on what it sees, so a prune justified by 'this option probably will not help' silently changes the result. The v0.5.426 dead-axis claim is cited there as the worked example of getting that wrong. STILL OPEN, and it is the task's real content: `hard_restart_frames` is carried per song and no term scores it, so its four-value second pass is chosen by nothing. evidence: **THE PLAN'S VERIFY IS POSED ON A PREMISE ITS OWN RUN LOG REFUTED BEFORE THE PLAN WAS WRITTEN, AND THE STALE TEXT IS MINE.** The verify says 'DONE WHEN the non-naming channel is identified ON POWERPLAY'. On that footing the naming share of Powerplay's loss is **67%, not 94%**: 3 attack renames (A#4->A-4 x2, D-5->C#5 x1), all within one semitone, recovering +1.92pp of 2.88pp, with 4 further attacks genuinely added or lost rather than renamed. #240 counted all 7 as renames; a strict positional difflib pairing supports 3. Same direction, materially different number, and the 94% is what the OPEN USER TASK powerplay-regrid-refusal-... quotes. **ONE_ON_ONE IS ~0% NAMING, WHICH IS THE SUCCESSOR QUESTION ANSWERED IN THE NEGATIVE.** melody 0.9864 -> 0.6162 (-37.03pp, reproduced), and the whole of it is voice 2 (0.9920 -> 0.4685; voice 0 moves 0.9890 -> 0.9832 and voice 1 0.9412 -> 0.8750 on 8 notes). Exactly ONE attack rename in the file (G#4->B-4, three semitones, not a boundary), and restoring it makes the score WORSE by 6.63pp. So the 71% figure #240 left standing for One_on_One is really ~100%: naming explains none of it. **THE DAMAGE IS THE DOUBLE-STRIKE PAIRING COMING APART.** This tune strikes every note twice -- the original has 372 attacks and 186 collapsed notes on voice 2, i.e. 186 repeated-attack pairs -- and the no-regrid arm reproduces that count EXACTLY (375 attacks, 189 collapsed, **186 repeated pairs against the original's 186**). With --regrid the repeated pairs fall to **160** while collapsed rises 189 -> 211 against the original's 186. Attacks fall TOWARD the original (375 -> 371 vs 372) while the collapsed sequence melody actually scores moves away from it, which is the signature of runs of identical attacks being broken up rather than of notes being renamed or lost.
verify_output: VERIFY NOT PASSED, AND IT CANNOT BE AS WRITTEN -- its target does not exist. Powerplay does not carry a non-naming channel worth identifying: 67% of its 2.88pp is naming by this run's measurement and 94% by #240's, and the residue either way is one or two attacks. What was run instead is the successor #240 named, and it returns a quantified answer: One_on_One voice 2, -37pp, ~0% naming, damage expressed as -26 repeated-attack pairs and +22 collapsed notes. REPRODUCTION FIRST, per this repo's rule and #240's own account of the run it lost: melody came from fidelity.compare() rather than a reimplementation, and the one quantity that HAD to be reimplemented (the score over a patched sequence, since compare() takes Voices) is asserted equal to compare()'s number on BOTH arms before use -- the probe aborts otherwise. MY FIRST VERSION FAILED THAT CHECK AND WOULD HAVE PUBLISHED A WRONG NUMBER: it invented a per-voice weighting by max(collapsed) where compare() weights by max(the ORIGINAL's UNCOLLAPSED attack count, 1). It matched the harness on the no-regrid arm by luck (0.9930) and missed the regrid arm (0.9608 vs 0.9643), and the near-miss on one arm is exactly what would have made it look trustworthy. Calibration was taken from table_calibration (-c10B8, detune -0.696), never re-derived -- the omission #240 records as costing it a run and reading 22% where the harness reads 99%. notes: DURABLE, DO NOT REDO: (1) the plan's DONE WHEN is refuted -- do not study the non-naming channel on Powerplay, there is at most one or two attacks of it there; (2) One_on_One voice 2 is the carrier and its damage is ~0% naming; (3) the run-structure numbers above (186/186 exact on the no-regrid arm, 160 with regrid, collapsed 189 -> 211).
